01 / ABOUT

Systems first, decoration second.

I'm Dika — a systems builder working where software engineering meets law and technology.

I care about how systems behave when things go wrong: explicit state, clear failure modes, and interfaces that stay usable on a small screen with a keyboard. Most of what I build ends up as web software, usually with TypeScript, React or Next.js.

The work is public on purpose. Every build here links to its source, says what is missing, and can be checked by someone who doesn't trust me.

BUILD LOG
3 published
  • Evidence over adjectives If it cannot be opened, run or read, it does not go on the page.
  • Boring where it counts Predictable state, explicit failure modes, no magic in the critical path.
  • Accessible by default Keyboard paths, focus states and contrast are part of the build, not a cleanup pass.

03 / WHAT I BUILD

Three things I keep coming back to.

Not a list of everything I have touched — a list of the work the case studies actually show.

01

Product interfaces

React and TypeScript interfaces that survive motion, small screens and keyboard-only use. State is explicit, so behaviour is predictable.

ReactTypeScriptTailwind
02

Static systems

Sites that ship as plain files: no runtime, no third-party requests unless they earn their place, and a build you can read in one sitting.

HTMLCSSGitHub Pages
03

Quality engineering

State machines, unit tests and automated accessibility checks — so behaviour is verified rather than assumed.

VitestPlaywrightaxe-core
